title: Grateful Dead Live at Capitol Theater on 1971-02-18
lineage: SBD > Dolby A Reel > Dolby A decode > DAT > Sound Forge NR > CD-R > SHN

ai_review.summary: Crystal‑clear soundboard capture of a historic 2/18/71 Capitol show highlighted by the legendary Wharf Rat → Dark Star sandwich and dozens of first‑time song debuts.
ai_review.review: The recording is a high‑fidelity soundboard source that most listeners describe as near‑perfect, with only a few complaints about noise‑reduction versions or isolated glitches. Musically the concert is a fire‑storm – the Wharf Rat/Dark Star “beautiful jam,” first performances of Bertha, Wharf Rat, Greatest Story Ever Told, Johnny B. Goode, Loser and Playing in the Band, plus tight runs through St. Stephen and Sugar Magnolia make it a must‑hear for any Deadhead.

ai_rating.rationale: Overwhelmingly high reviewer stars (majority 5) and enthusiastic comments about both performance and sound quality outweigh a handful of low‑star technical complaints.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Crisp, clear mix praised by many; occasional criticism of noise‑reduction version and an isolated glitch at ~2:22 on one track, but overall regarded as near‑perfect.

poor_songs: "Playin'" noted by a few as weak
show_quality.setlist_flow: A landmark Capitol set with two halves packed with first‑time songs; seamless transitions, especially the Wharf Rat/Dark Star sandwich, give the show a narrative arc that feels both historic and tightly paced.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Repeatedly praised for soaring, articulate guitar work and the “beautiful jam” – described as one of his most inspired performances.
band_member_comments.Phil: Mentioned as moved to tears by the beautiful jam; occasional “Phil bombs” references implied strong bass presence.
band_member_comments.Keys: Ned Lagin noted on Casey Jones, providing a distinctive keyboard texture for this era.
